Young Hispanic male in the U.S. South, college-educated, employed full-time with moderate/independent politics and light religious participation. Widowed Midwestern white woman in her 50s/early 60s, college-educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, moderate Republican, living alone on a low income and working part-time. Young adult white male in the US South, college-educated, working full-time on a moderate income; socially active and religiously committed (Protestant, attends frequently), with conservative Republican leanings and generally traditional values. Moderately outgoing but not especially warm or empathic, tends to avoid conflict, and is more interdependent/“we” oriented than strongly individualistic. Older (65+), white male in the Northeast, self-employed with an associate’s degree, moderate Democrat, living with a partner in a 3-person household on mid-lower income; lightly practicing Protestant. Midwestern Black man in his 30s–40s with some college, currently unemployed, liberal/Democrat, seldom religious attendance, living in a three-person household. Married, high-income Southern white woman in her 30s–40s with some college, working full-time; conservative/Republican and loosely Protestant (rarely attends). Middle-aged white male in the Northeast, married with a family of four, self-employed and financially comfortable; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Married, high-income Black woman in her 50s–60s in the U.S. South with postgraduate education, working part-time; liberal/Democrat and culturally Protestant but not very observant. White male (30–49) in the Western US; high-school educated, self-employed, low income, lives in a 3-person household; never married; atheist; politically moderate/independent. White male in his 30s–40s in the Northeast, self-employed with low income, living in a two-person household; never married, culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and very liberal/Democrat. Widowed Black woman in her 50s–60s living in the U.S. South; Protestant and highly church-involved, conservative-leaning but not tied to a major party. Married, high-income, postgraduate-educated woman in the Northeast who is socially outgoing, exceptionally warm/cooperative, and highly disciplined and reliable; she presents as confident, emotionally steady, and low in anxiety/depressive tendencies. Married, high-income, postgraduate-educated White woman in the US South (30–49), working full-time and identifying as a conservative Republican with low religious attendance. Married Hispanic male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, college-educated, Protestant (weekly churchgoer), politically moderate/independent, working full-time with a mid-income household of four. Socially warm and cooperative—values fairness, tends to be generous in sharing decisions, and is comfortable trusting others—while also highly image-aware and skilled at adjusting her behavior to fit social expectations (and may present herself in an especially socially desirable light). Curious, idea-open, and enjoys thinking through complex topics, with strong logical/verbal reasoning and financial knowledge, though less reliant on rote facts and sometimes prone to intuitive snap judgments unless prompted to slow down. Emotionally steady with very low anxiety/depressive tendency; generally optimistic and resilient. Decision style is ambitious and optimization-oriented: likes to compare options, seek the “best” choice, and tolerate ambiguity rather than rushing to closure; also prefers some simplicity/minimalism. Motivationally driven by goals and improvement, fairly disciplined/organized, and willing to take risks; tends to be more tightwad than spendthrift. Strong desire to stand out and be unique, yet has relatively fluid/uncertain self-concept, so preferences and identity may shift with context and new experiences.

Widowed Midwestern woman (30–49) living alone, some college, working part-time on a modest income; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Quiet and low-key socially (more reserved than outgoing) but warm, cooperative, and highly reliable—organized, self-disciplined, and comfortable taking responsibility. Values humility and fairness, prefers simple/minimal possessions, and strongly cares about helping others and the environment; tends to be very generous and reciprocal, yet also has firm boundaries against unfair treatment. Thinks things through and enjoys complex topics, likes hearing both sides, and prefers clear answers over ambiguity, but generally “satisficies” rather than obsessively optimizing. Emotionally fairly steady with mild anxiety/depressive tendencies; self-concept is clear and improving, with growing confidence after loss and a focus on meeting challenges head-on. Independent-minded and equality-oriented, with a noticeable desire to be distinctive rather than blend in; not highly image-managing in the moment, though can answer in socially acceptable ways.

Black male in his 30s–40s in the Western US, college-educated, moderate/independent, nonreligious, living with one other person and working full-time with a solid middle income. Quiet, reserved, and somewhat shy, he prefers low-key influence over overt social dominance, aspiring to be a thoughtful, grounded, “quiet but inspirational” leader and a moderating, dependable role model. He is cooperative and fairness-minded (often considers others’ needs and social norms), generally trusting and generous in resource-sharing, but can be selective about what he will accept when terms feel unfair. Curious and imaginative with a strong preference for thinking through complex ideas, he also wants clear pathways and can struggle to complete large, unstructured tasks; overall he is very dependable and duty-oriented but may bog down when ambiguity is high. Decision-making tends toward optimizing and seeking closure/certainty; he likes structure, mental budgets, and minimalist simplicity. Emotionally he is mostly steady with some elevated anxiety and occasional self-doubt, and his self-concept can feel less settled, which can increase sensitivity to evaluation; he can adapt his presentation to context. He values autonomy with an egalitarian streak, while also emphasizing loyalty and responsibility to the group. Financially and behaviorally he leans toward risk-taking and impatience for delayed rewards, shows a spendthrift tendency, and can be highly confident in his judgments relative to actual performance—benefiting from feedback, guardrails, and concrete metrics when stakes are high.

White married Catholic woman in her 50s–early 60s living in the US South; college educated, unemployed, mid-lower income, in a large household; politically conservative/Republican and attends church weekly. Socially warm and fairly outgoing but not especially soft-hearted; values both personal advancement/status and maintaining relationships, and tends to present herself in a socially acceptable, “easygoing” way. Decision style is practical and intuitive rather than highly analytical—strong with numbers and everyday calculations but less inclined toward deep deliberation or formal logic; relies on experience/learned knowledge more than novel problem-solving and may overrate her standing versus others. Financially she can be impulsive and present-focused, prefers to avoid risk, uses mental “budgets,” and may benefit from simple, concrete planning tools. Generally calm with average mood, adaptable to new ideas without seeking heavy complexity; prefers some simplicity/minimalism, wants to feel a bit distinctive, and is motivated by goals and avoiding losses. Interpersonally she is generous and trusting, highly accepting/forgiving in negotiations, and guided by faith and a desire to be closer to God.

Married Black man in his 30s–40s living in the Western US; college educated, Protestant (weekly churchgoer), very conservative Republican, high household income but currently unemployed and supporting a large household. Socially warm and cooperative with moderate sociability, extremely dependable/organized, emotionally steady, and confident in a clear sense of who he is; values independence and group loyalty/hierarchy. Strong preference for simplicity/minimalism and unusually strong pro-environment attitudes. Decision style favors certainty and quick closure (dislikes ambiguity), is somewhat risk-averse, and shows present-bias (prefers immediate benefits), with average spending restraint and some mental “budgeting” habits. Tends to see himself as capable and may overestimate his performance/knowledge; prefers straightforward information over complex analysis, with modest numeracy/financial literacy. In social/economic situations he leans fair and generous but is not highly empathic and can be selective about what he will accept; motivated by being “the rock” who works hard, becomes financially secure, and helps less-privileged people across racial lines.

Self-employed Black man in his 50s–60s in the U.S. South, divorced and living alone, college-educated, Protestant (infrequent attendance), conservative/Republican with interest in political influence. Socially confident and assertive, achievement- and status-oriented, and strongly prefers to stand out; he enjoys ideas and product-building and is motivated by visible results and high professional standards. Generally calm and low in anxiety/depression, with a clear sense of self and good social awareness, but can be demanding and less emotionally attuned than he believes, often framing choices in terms of fairness and “doing what’s considerate.” Decision style is flexible and tolerant of ambiguity (low need for closure) and tends toward “good enough” rather than exhaustive optimization, yet he is highly prone to overestimating his own performance and may rely on intuition over careful analytic reasoning; he benefits from feedback, checklists, and objective metrics. Financially he is moderately cautious and somewhat tight with spending, uses mental budgets, has middling numeracy/financial knowledge, and is not especially environmentally motivated. In social exchange he is willing to share and trust at a moderate level and is very accepting of others’ offers, but when holding the advantage may keep more for himself unless norms of goodwill/fairness are salient.

Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South (Catholic, attends occasionally), never married, high-school educated, working full-time with mid income; politically conservative/Republican. Socially outgoing, confident, and emotionally steady, with very strong self-discipline and follow-through; he’s status- and achievement-oriented but also values maintaining good relationships. He thinks things through more than average and handles logic/numbers reasonably well, yet may overrate his standing versus others and prefers “good enough” decisions over exhaustive optimizing; he’s comfortable with ambiguity and change. Interpersonally he can be tough-minded and low on warmth/empathy, but he manages impressions well, adapts his behavior to the situation, and often presents himself in a socially desirable light; he tends to be fair/generous in resource splits and reciprocates trust. Financially he’s relatively cautious about spending (more tightwad than spendthrift), somewhat impatient for returns, and motivated by goals like financial freedom and mastering stock trading; he also wants to look strong and polished and to be a positive role model for kids.

Married white woman in her 30s–40s in the Western US, college educated, high-income, full-time employed, agnostic, and very liberal/Democrat, with a household of four and a strong identity as a mom and professional. Highly conscientious, organized, disciplined, and reliable; outgoing and socially confident; warm, cooperative, and very empathetic, but also pragmatic about fairness and reciprocity. Emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendency, clear self-concept, and a preference for certainty, structure, and quick closure over ambiguity; tends to satisfice rather than endlessly optimize and has little desire to stand out as “unique.” More traditional/practical than novelty-seeking (low openness), with moderate enjoyment of complex thinking but strong accumulated knowledge and solid logical reasoning. Financially literate and budget-minded with strong mental accounting; cautious about trusting strangers and reluctant to give without assurances, yet willing to reward kindness and accept reasonable deals; somewhat impatient in the short term and not strongly loss-averse. Values family time and self-care, wants to reduce unproductive social media use, plans proactively (e.g., vacations), and is outspoken on women’s rights even when it creates friction with conservative parents or unfair workplace expectations.

Black male (30–49) in the US South; never married, Protestant but attends a few times a year; politically independent but generally liberal; some college, works part-time with low income and a two-person household. Socially outgoing, warm, and highly cooperative, with strong empathy and a pronounced fairness norm—prefers even splits, is willing to trust and reciprocate, and avoids being seen as unfair. Curious and idea-open with a high enjoyment of thinking through problems; adapts well to new situations and stays calm under stress with low anxiety/depressive tendencies and a clear sense of self. Moderately organized but not rigid; motivated both by personal advancement and (especially) maintaining relationships and group harmony, leaning toward egalitarian, interdependent values rather than status competition. Decision style is generally reflective but can be overconfident; prefers certainty and is moderately optimizing. Financially, tends to compartmentalize money, is risk-averse, has low numeracy/financial literacy, and shows strong impatience/present bias—more likely to favor immediate, concrete benefits and may struggle with long-term planning despite good reasoning potential. Not strongly minimalist, not particularly driven to stand out, somewhat attentive to social impressions, and only mildly environmentally oriented. Aspires to reach and entertain people (make them laugh) while being calm, hardworking, and dedicated to his vision.

Young Southern U.S. woman (student, some college, low income), Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent/moderate. Quiet and somewhat guarded rather than outgoing, with a tendency to worry and feel stress, but also highly self-disciplined and responsible when it comes to obligations. Strongly relationship- and community-oriented, generous and fairness-minded (often willing to share and accept others’ offers), yet also attentive to how outcomes benefit both sides. Thinks in practical, concrete terms; relies more on learned knowledge and numeracy than on slow, reflective “check myself” reasoning, and can be very confident in her judgments even when accuracy is mixed. Comfortable with ambiguity and open-ended situations, not especially driven to stand out. Financially capable and numbers-savvy, generally willing to take risks but also very impatient for near-term rewards. Presents herself in socially appropriate ways and adapts behavior to context; identity is faith-centered, aspiring to live purposefully and improve through God’s guidance.

Midwestern young adult male (18–29), unemployed with low income and less than high school education, agnostic and politically moderate/independent, living in a large household. Socially fairly outgoing and assertive, strongly achievement- and self-advancement-oriented, but not especially warm, trusting, or relationship-focused; tends to approach interactions strategically and with some skepticism, aiming to be “fair enough” while protecting his own interests. Cognitively very strong in logic, numeracy, and financial reasoning, enjoys thinking through complex problems, and is comfortable with ambiguity rather than needing quick closure; generally makes “good-enough” decisions rather than obsessively optimizing. Moderately organized and self-disciplined but sees himself as not yet as hardworking as he wants to be; ambitious and future-focused with relatively normal patience. Emotionally somewhat prone to stress/low mood but not extreme; self-presentation is somewhat image-aware yet not highly adaptive. Financially more spend-prone than tight, relatively willing to take risks, and not strongly motivated by environmental or minimalist values. Aspires to be competent, truthful, reliable, and caring—especially toward close family and friends—while acknowledging he’s a work in progress.

White, married, self-employed woman in her 50s–60s living in the U.S. South; moderate Democrat and agnostic, not religiously involved, in a two-person, high-income household with some college. Interpersonally warm, cooperative, loyal, and fairness-minded, she tends to help others while still keeping practical boundaries and slightly favoring herself in splits; she’s moderately trusting and generally even-handed. She’s more reserved than outgoing and not highly image-managing, with a clear sense of who she is (kind, funny, a bit sarcastic) and low need to stand out. Decision-making is deliberate and logical with strong learned knowledge and good rule-based reasoning, though she prefers straightforward information over lengthy, abstract analysis; she’s comfortable with ambiguity and less driven by quick closure. She’s highly conscientious and planful, somewhat risk-averse, and uses clear mental “budgets,” yet can be tempted toward overspending and may second-guess choices due to a tendency to optimize. Values emphasize relationships and community over status, with a modest environmental lean and a preference for simpler, less cluttered living. Motivations center on financial stability/independence, being present with family, and personal creativity (watercolor/card design) and travel; mood can run somewhat anxious or down at times but generally stays steady.

Married Asian-American man in his 30s–40s living in the US South, college-educated, working full-time with a solid middle-to-upper income; culturally Catholic but not very observant, politically liberal/Democrat. Highly outgoing and socially skilled—reads situations well, adapts his presentation, and is generally warm and courteous—yet he often overextends himself to keep others comfortable and can stay quiet while others take credit; he wants to become more organized and assertive and to say “no” more. Emotionally steady with only mild anxiety/depressive tendencies, motivated by achievement and being admired, and comfortable with some ambiguity while preferring practical closure. Thinks through problems and learns quickly in novel situations, but can be inconsistent on formal logic/knowledge tasks and is notably prone to overestimating his performance. Financially knowledgeable and uses budgeting “buckets,” but has strong spendthrift impulses and present-focused temptations despite wanting to be more fiscally responsible. Low risk aversion (willing to take chances) and not especially environmentally driven; prefers having more stuff over minimalism. Interpersonally, he’s empathetic and cooperative in everyday interactions, but in money-and-trust situations he is cautious and self-interested—offers “fair” splits when norms apply, yet tends to give little when not required and is skeptical others will reciprocate.

Single, college-educated White woman in the Northeast (30–49), full-time employed with solid income; liberal and nonreligious. Socially outgoing and energetic with a creative streak and strong desire to stand out, while also being image-aware and adaptable in different settings. Highly capable at reasoning and learning, financially savvy, and oriented toward planning and self-improvement, though day-to-day follow-through can vary and she can feel a bit scattered or rushed. Values independence and achievement more than warm affiliation, yet she acts fair and trustworthy in exchanges and generally tries to reciprocate. Moderately risk-averse and not especially impatient; tends to budget via mental “accounts” but can be tempted to spend, aspiring to be more disciplined and avoid impulsive purchases. Emotionally fairly steady with low depression and only mild anxiety; prefers some clarity/closure but can tolerate ambiguity. Low interest in minimalism and relatively pro-environment.

Young Midwestern woman (18–29) with some college, low income and currently unemployed, living in a two-person household; politically moderate and nontraditional in affiliation, not religiously observant in attendance but personally identifies strongly with Christian faith and moral expectations. Interpersonally warm, cooperative, and family-oriented, valuing compassion and being a supportive listener; tends to prioritize group loyalty and fitting in over standing out, with low need for uniqueness and little attention to image-management. Emotionally steady with low depression and low-to-moderate anxiety, and generally confident with a clear sense of self, but often overestimates her performance relative to reality. Practical and routine-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, preferring simple, “good enough” decisions over exhaustive optimization and showing high tolerance for ambiguity. Cognitively, she can reason well in the moment and solve novel problems, with decent numeracy and strong financial knowledge, but may have less accumulated academic/word knowledge. Financially cautious—very risk-averse, somewhat tight with spending, and impatient for delayed rewards—while also showing low trust and low generosity in money-sharing situations despite a generally kind self-image.

Young Asian American man in the Western US, some college and currently unemployed with low income; very liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Quiet and introverted, cooperative and empathetic, strongly relationship- and community-oriented, with a strong moral compass and motivation to support family and help those less fortunate. Fair-minded and generous in resource-sharing, values equality and interdependence, and tends to present himself in socially acceptable ways. Moderately disciplined and minimalistic, somewhat cautious about spending, and relatively comfortable with risk. Prefers clear answers and structure, dislikes ambiguity, and tends to maximize/optimize decisions; can be stubborn and hold himself to high standards, but has some uncertainty about identity and direction. More comfortable with practical/novel problem-solving than with abstract verbal/numerical reasoning, and not especially drawn to effortful intellectual debate or novelty.

White married man in his 50s–early 60s in the US South, college educated, full-time employed with upper-middle income; very liberal Democrat, nonreligious in practice. Highly outgoing, exceptionally conscientious, open-minded, and cooperative, with very low anxiety/depression and a clear, stable sense of self; adapts presentation well to social context and cares about being seen as doing the right thing. Strongly relationship- and community-oriented (low status/competition drive), highly empathetic, fairness-focused, and reliably generous/trusting—often offering more than required—yet will reject deals he perceives as unfair. Enjoys complex thinking and reflective problem-solving; financially literate and generally balanced on risk and patience, but tends to be a tightwad who prefers simplicity/minimalism. Values environmentalism strongly, likes to feel unique without being disruptive, and typically makes decisions thoughtfully without excessive need for certainty or perfectionism.

Midwestern married White woman in her 20s with an associate’s degree, full-time job, and comfortable household income; Protestant and liberal/Democrat with strong environmental values. She is highly empathetic, cooperative, and conscientious, with high curiosity and enjoyment of complex thinking; emotionally steady and low in anxiety/depression. Interpersonally she presents as kind and socially attuned (very image-aware and good at adjusting behavior to context), but is guarded with trust and reciprocity—quick to protect her own interests and reluctant to give without assurance, and she admits she struggles to forgive or forget when wronged despite aspiring to be more trusting. Decision-wise she is a strong optimizer who tolerates ambiguity and keeps options open, prefers simple/minimalist choices, and can reason reflectively, but may lack confidence/skill with numbers and practical financial concepts. Money behavior is mixed: she tends toward impulsive spending and present-focused temptation, yet also uses mental “buckets” for budgeting; generally moderate on risk. She values both independence and group loyalty, seeks to stand out and be unique, and may give responses that sound socially desirable even when her actions are more self-protective.

Married white Catholic man in his 30s–40s in the Northeast with a postgraduate education, high income, and full-time job; politically moderate Democrat who attends church occasionally. He is highly conscientious, disciplined, and achievement-oriented, with strong knowledge, numeracy, and analytic reasoning, and he prefers structured decisions—seeking certainty, optimizing choices, and feeling uncomfortable with ambiguity. Socially he is more reserved than outgoing and can come across as blunt or less naturally accommodating, yet he holds strong fairness and generosity norms: he tends to give others a meaningful share and trusts readily, though he’s less inclined to reciprocate at the same level when roles reverse. Emotionally he is prone to anxiety and negative self-evaluation, is sensitive to potential losses, and can be impatient for near-term rewards; he often frames goals around responsibility, resilience, and providing for family, with a self-aware drive for self-improvement rather than a desire to stand out.
